description: Add timeout wrapping and degraded status logic to /health/deep endpoint in the backend. Currently, slow probes (especially vertex_search warm_up) can make the entire deep health check timeout. Add asyncio.wait_for with 5s timeout to each probe, and implement degraded logic: only return 503 if core services (mongodb, redis) are down; if only non-critical services (vertex_search, vertex_ai) are unhealthy, return 200 with status 'degraded'.
steps: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/health.py, add 'import asyncio' at the top

Add a helper function '_safe_check(coro, timeout=5.0)' that wraps a coroutine with asyncio.wait_for. On TimeoutError, return {'status': 'unhealthy', 'error': 'timeout'}. On other exceptions, return {'status': 'unhealthy', 'error': str(e)}.
In the deep_health_check function, replace the direct await calls with _safe_check wrappers: e.g. 'mongodb': await _safe_check(mongo_ping()), 'redis': await _safe_check(redis_ping()), etc.

Change the overall status logic: define CORE_SERVICES = {'mongodb', 'redis'} and NON_CRITICAL_SERVICES = {'vertex_search', 'vertex_ai'}. If any core service is unhealthy, return 503 with status 'unhealthy'. If only non-critical services are unhealthy, return 200 with status 'degraded'. If all healthy, return 200 with status 'healthy'.
Keep the response format compatible: still return {'status': ..., 'checks': {...}}
acceptance_criteria: Each health probe is wrapped with a 5-second asyncio timeout
A single slow probe no longer blocks the entire endpoint indefinitely
If only vertex_search or vertex_ai is unhealthy/timed out, HTTP 200 is returned with status 'degraded'
If mongodb or redis is unhealthy, HTTP 503 is returned with status 'unhealthy'
If all services are healthy, HTTP 200 is returned with status 'healthy'
Existing test test_health_deep_endpoint_accessible still passes (it checks status != 500)
verification: Run: cd /projects/sandbox/-kalukaliya/apps/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_endpoints_audit.py -x -v to confirm health tests pass
Run: cd /projects/sandbox/-kalukaliya/apps/backend && python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('app/api/v1/health.py').read())" to confirm syntax is valid
